newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, Zagrebacka seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, Zagrebacka seen rising.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Thursday in very active trade, with Zagrebacka Banka accounting for most of the day's deals and traders expecting a further rise in the price of its shares.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka sold 12,061 shares and added 95 kuna or 4.8 percent to 2,095 kuna.

"There is a good chance it will rise further on Friday," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage ascribing its good performance to the solid rise of its Global Depository Receipts (GDR) in London where they fetched $33.625 by mid-afternoon.
Traders earlier said a strong dollar had helped Zagrebacka's recovery.
Kos foresaw stagnation for most other issues.
Six of the 18 stocks traded on Thursday rose, seven fell and five were flat. Volume rose to 34,947 from 24,753 units, while turnover almost tripled to 34.9 million kuna.
Top gainer was ship repair company Viktor Lenac adding 13 kuna or 11.2 percent to 129 kuna on volume of 1,900 shares.
The company on Tuesday joined Zagrebacka, drugs firm Pliva and Varazdinska banka in the top bracket of the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
Pliva shares dropped by a single kuna to 500 and traded 1,291 shares.
"Pliva is experiencing a momentary standstill," Kos commented.

Varazdinska banka A-series was the third most active issue with 10,754 shares sold, closing flat at 210 kuna. A trader said the bank sold a package of 10,000 shares for 200 kuna to one buyer at the beginning of the session.
Food processor Podravka was the biggest decliner losing five kuna or 2.0 percent to 245 kuna with 10,859 shares sold.
"The situation in Podravka right now is the result of some speculative investment," said Kos.
Podravka was a rare attraction in the dormant Croatian market last week, with its price forging ahead, but edged down at the start of this week's trading.
